A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MENTOR and retain matching methods, experiments and case studies. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three model backbones, benchmark results in Table 1, training and reasoning analyses in Figures 2–4, and trajectory case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and additionally reports guidance comparisons, component and hyperparameter ablations, and training-efficiency measurements in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The proposed entropy-weighted mixture, speculative rollout procedure and mixed-policy GRPO objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 provides fuller training-loop documentation; the random and perplexity guidance procedures are introduced as comparison variants rather than changes to default MENTOR.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MATH and simplified OpenR1 training coverage and the same nine evaluation benchmarks in Table 1. Minerva, Olympiad and ARC already appear in v1. The added analyses reuse existing mathematics tasks rather than introduce new domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Base, On-policy RL, LUFFY and QuestA. v2 additionally evaluates random and perplexity-based guidance in Table 2 and separately evaluates DAPO in the efficiency comparison, Table 6. v1's use of DAPO's Clip-Higher within its on-policy baseline is distinct from this additional comparator.

E3.justification: The main training and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added protocols include AIME24 guidance-token collection at temperature 1.0, controlled expert-weight and entropy-quantile sweeps, and a 200-step efficiency comparison measuring stage runtimes and gradient-producing tokens per second.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F add substantial diagnostic evidence absent from v1: alternative guidance selection and token distributions, progressive component ablation, fixed versus decaying expert weights, entropy-threshold sensitivity, and computational-efficiency analysis. The earlier training-dynamics, reasoning-pattern, pass@32 and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates; averaging runtimes over training steps does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical results and Figures 2–4 are unchanged, but Tables 2–6 add substantial results. Examples include random/perplexity guidance scores of 77.6/77.0 on MATH and 14.8/13.3 on AIME24, rollout-only scores of 79.4/14.6, and MENTOR timing of 627 seconds per step with throughput of 2860 tokens/s. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's same-setting results.

T1.justification: Definition 2.2 changes the reward maximum from the current exploration support to the global sequence space, allowing the explorable optimal subset to be empty. v2 adds Theorem 2.1 and its entropy-bound derivation, plus Appendix A.3's argument for filtering misleading guidance and a GRPO performance lower bound. The speculative-sampling proof is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: selective expert guidance improves effective and diverse exploration, avoids superficial imitation, and improves benchmark performance and reasoning coverage. The new analyses support these retained claims without redefining the headline contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations connecting optimal-set size to entropy decay, claiming automatic protection against misleading experts, explaining why guidance selection and weight decay matter, and characterizing computational overhead as acceptable. These extend v1's interpretations considerably. Some are overstated: Appendix E.2 claims improvement under every weight setting despite Table 4's fixed-alpha=1 AIME24 score falling below GRPO.

D1.justification: New Algorithm 2 documents the complete training loop, including old-policy refresh and entropy-threshold updates. The added experiments disclose guidance-selection parameters and runtime measurements. Section 9 adds a code/data availability statement and a planned checkpoint release. Existing hardware, prompts, reward design and main hyperparameters are largely retained from v1 Appendix B in v2 Appendix C.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a focused discussion of confidence-based reasoning and process-verifier search, contrasting exploration within a model's distribution with stronger-expert guidance. It adds works including Tree of Thoughts, Deep Think with Confidence and process-supervision approaches, while dropping Wu et al.'s strategy-selection-bias reference. The central positioning against expert-trajectory imitation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing abstract, introduction, method, results and conclusion prose is retained. Local changes include rewriting Section 2.2, expanding the opening of Section 3.1, correcting duplicated wording, revising author/header information, adding declarations, and reorganizing the appendices around new material.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial set of displays: guidance-token word clouds in Figure 5, comparison and ablation Tables 2–5, efficiency Table 6, and full-training Algorithm 2. It also adopts the ICLR layout and reflows existing material, including placing Table 1 and Figure 2 together. Existing figures and case-study displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The new controlled ablations and runtime measurements address v1's limited evidence for specific design choices and computational cost, while preserving its main results. The gain is tempered by new inconsistencies: Equation (7) uses log(N/K), whereas Appendix A.1 derives log((N-K)/K), and the universal-improvement claim conflicts with Table 4's AIME24 result of 13.9 versus GRPO's 14.2. Overall, empirical support improves more convincingly than theoretical rigor.
